Well I never had a reason to go to Kansas anyway, but now I will be consciously avoiding it.
When I think of Kansas and guns, I think of John Brown.
When I think of John Brown, I think of this.
When I think of that, I think of this.
If you live in an area where you need a gun to feel safe you should probably move somewhere more civilized.

Not everyone has a choice or means to do so. Ever heard of Gary, Indiana? Such a crime filled cesspool. Industry went under, those who could get out got out. The rest are stuck and are either driven to crime or are forced to live among crime. In a world ruled by money, just moving to "somewhere more civilized" is not an option to all people. I know if I was unfortunate enough to be in Gary, I'd want a gun with me no matter where I was.

I'm not like super progun but I'm not anti-gun either and when people make comments like "ZOMG law abiding citizens can now carry guns w/o a permit! Oh the hunanity!" I wonder if they have ever considered the reality that CRIMINALS have had it that way forever. I don't feel safer because of more guns in civilian hands though... but still think its unfair to outcry against normal people being allowed to arm themselves.
And without training. Nice! What could go wrong?

A couple points to the people who say things like "Now I'll never go to Kansas".

1 Pretty good chance that you were never going to Kansas in the first place

2 Have you ever been to Kansas? I have many times and gun violence is not something you worry about. A bigger concern is whether to eat Oklahoma's Joes or Arthur Bryant's.

Kansas has 2.2 gun murders per 100,000 people and 42% of the population owns a gun. DC has 16.5 gun murders per 100,000 and 3.6% of the population owns a gun. There is not a correlation between states with loose gun laws and high crime.
